summary: Raafi bin Khadeej relates that Abu Ubaydah and Umar pleaded with Qais bin Sa'd not to slaughter more camels, but he did so to feed the army during the Expedition of Leaves, and the Prophet praised him as being from the house of generosity.
notes: Text spells the narrator 'Raafl bin Khudayj' (OCR); matched to raafi-bin-khadeej.

summary: Jaabir relates how Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah slaughtered seven camels to feed the hungry army, and how they then found a giant fish on the shore that sustained them for three days.

Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that when Umar reached Shaam, Bilaal rebuked him that the commanders ate well while the Muslims under them were ill fed, and Umar made each commander guarantee provision for every Muslim under his command.
notes: Qais bin Abu Haazim is not in the vocabulary and the text does not say whether he was a Companion.

summary: Abdullaah Howzini relates Bilaal's account of the Prophet's finances: Bilaal borrowed on his behalf to help the destitute, a creditor pressed him, and four camels sent as a gift from Fidak let him settle every debt; the Prophet then gave away what remained rather than die with wealth in his possession.
notes: The mushrik creditor is unnamed. Abdullaah Howzini is not in the vocabulary and his sahabi status is not stated.

summary: Ummu Salama describes how a bag of eight hundred dirhams reached the Prophet at night, and how he kept breaking off his salaah to think about it until he had distributed all of it at dawn.
notes: Text breaks off mid-sentence after 'return to my'.

summary: Abu Moosa relates that Alaa bin Hadhrami sent eighty thousand from Bahrain; the Prophet gave it out on a mat without counting, and when Abbaas, who had paid his own and Aqeel's ransom after Badr, asked for a share, the Prophet let him take as much as he could carry.
Sahl bin Abi Hathma reports that Abu Bakr kept the public treasury unguarded because it had a lock, distributed all of it, and after his death Umar's trusted men found only a single dirham in it.
notes: Opening words 'as Khali fall' are OCR debris. The man who weighed the wealth is unnamed.

summary: Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad reports that Abu Bakr gave everyone equal shares; when Umar objected about the Badr veterans, Abu Bakr said worldly provision should be equal and the Badr veterans' superiority would show in their reward in the Aakhirah.

Three further reports show Abu Bakr refusing to favour any group in distribution: virtue is rewarded by Allaah in the Aakhirah and equality suits worldly life, and he asked whether he should buy the Muhaajireen's precedence from them, while Umar's objections are recorded.
notes: Contains three separate reports: an unnamed first narrator, Aslam, and Amr bin Abdullaah. The text also ends mid-word at 'W'.

summary: Umar bin Abdullaah, freed slave of Ghafra, reports that after the Prophet's death wealth came from Bahrain; Abu Bakr paid Jaabir the handfuls the Prophet had promised him, then gave every person ten dirhams, and twenty the following year, refusing to favour the early Muhaajireen and Ansaar.
notes: Ends by pointing to the next chapter ('the rest of the narration will soon be quoted'). The Ibn Sa'd citation footnote is editorial and left out.

summary: Umar, as Khalifah, sets the allowances by precedence in Islaam and closeness to the Prophet, giving Badr veterans and their sons more, and answers the objections of Safiyya, Juwayriyya, Talha, Muhammad bin Abdullaah bin Jahash and his own son Abdullaah.
notes: 'Nadhar bin Anas' is probably the son of Anas bin Nadhar, but the approved anas-bin-nadhar is the father named in the Uhud story, so it is left unmatched. Juwayriyya, Ubaydullaah and Abdullaah bin Jahash are not in the vocabulary. Safiyya is matched to safiyya-bint-abdul-muttalib. The text ends by saying the rest of the narration will follow, which is the next item.

summary: Anas bin Maalik and Sa'eed bin Musayyib report that Umar's allowances were five thousand for the Muhaajireen, four thousand for the Ansaar and four thousand for the sons of Muhaajireen who missed Badr, and that Abdullaah bin Umar refused a share he had no right to.
notes: The ﷺ after 'Muhammad' in the text is OCR debris: the person is Muhammad bin Abdullaah bin Jahash, not the Prophet. The OCR gives 'Rahmaan bin Auf' for the speaker, matched to abdur-rahmaan-bin-awf.

summary: Zaid bin Aslam relates that Umar gave Abdullaah, son of Handhala, two thousand, more than Talha's Muhaajir cousin, because of his father Handhala's courage at Uhud; the report breaks off mid-sentence.
notes: Text breaks off mid-sentence ('deflect enemy swords and'). Handhala is not matched to handhala-bin-raahib or handhala-bin-rabee-tameemi, which name different people. Talha's cousin is unnamed.

summary: Naashira bin Sumay Yazani reports Umar's lecture at Jaabiya: he gave the Muhaajireen of Badr the most, the Ansaar of Badr less and the Uhud fighters three thousand, gave all the Prophet's wives an equal amount after Aa'isha pointed out the Prophet treated them equally, and defended removing Khaalid bin Waleed from command, which Abu Amr bin Hafs disputed.
notes: Juwayriyya and Maymoona are not in the vocabulary. Abu Amr bin Hafs is not matched to abu-amr-bin-himaas and his sahabi status is not stated.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports bringing Umar eight hundred thousand dirhams from Abu Moosa; Umar checked that it was lawful and stayed awake all night, then consulted the Sahabah and had a register drawn up, starting with the Prophet's family and the Banu Haashim.
notes: Abu Hurayrah is the narrator and also the one who acts in his own account, so tagged as subject.

summary: Jubayr bin Huwayrith reports that Umar consulted on keeping a register; after Uthmaan and Waleed bin Hishaam urged it, Umar had Aqeel, Makhrama bin Naufal and Jubayr bin Mut'im record people by status, starting with the Prophet and his kin, and then Abu Bakr's tribe and his own.
notes: The advisor who proposed annual distribution is garbled in the text ('Hadhrat (RA) advisedhim') and is left unnamed. Waleed bin Hishaam is not matched to waleed-bin-mughiera. Makhrama bin Naufal and Jubayr bin Mut'im are not in the vocabulary.

summary: Aslam reports that when Umar put his own tribe after Abu Bakr's, the Banu Adi called him the successor of Rasulullaah; Umar corrected them that he succeeded Abu Bakr, and said honour comes only through the Prophet and reward only through deeds, not lineage.

Umar bin Abdullaah, freed slave of Ghafra, repeats the report of wealth from Bahrain after the Prophet's death, and Umar's Jumu'ah address answers rumours of a quick pledge after his death: he would switch to Abu Bakr's equal distribution if he lived.
notes: Opens by referring back to the previous narration and ends with 'The narration still continues further.'

summary: Hasan reports that after Umar had distributed the money, some remained, and Abbaas argued that as the uncle of the Prophet he deserved it more than the uncle of Musa, so Umar gave the rest to Abbaas.
notes: The narrator is only 'Hadhrat Hasan' in the text, so he is not matched to hasan or hasan-bin-ali. Musa is named as the prophet.

summary: Aa'isha relates that Umar sent her a perfume container, asking permission because of the Prophet's love for her; she remarked on how many conquests Umar had made after the Prophet and prayed not to live to see his next gift.
notes: Aa'isha is the narrator telling her own experience, so tagged as subject.

summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that Abu Bakr had sent him to collect zakaah, Abu Bakr died before he returned, and Umar let him keep the four thousand collected, making him the richest person in Madinah.
notes: Anas is the narrator telling his own story, so tagged as subject.

summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr relates that Umar gave a wounded man four thousand dirhams in four instalments; when the man left embarrassed, Umar said he would have kept giving until nothing was left, because of the scar from his wound in the path of Allaah.
notes: The wounded man is unnamed.

summary: Ali distributes the wealth from Isfahaan three times a year and, announcing that he is not their treasurer, gives away everything, even the ropes that held the animals.
notes: The name is lost to OCR in the body ('Hadhrat (RA) bin Abi Taalib'); tagged as ali from the section heading 'Hadhrat Ali (RA) Distributes Wealth'. No narrator is named.

summary: Sa'eed narrates that Umar ordered the treasurer Abdullaah bin Arqam to distribute the Baytul Maal monthly, then weekly, then daily, and rejected a suggestion to keep a reserve as Shaytaan speaking, saying he would follow the Prophet's preparation of obedience to Allaah and His Rasool.
notes: The narrator is only 'Hadhrat Sa'eed' and is not matched to saeed-bin-musayyab. Abdullaah bin Arqam is not the approved arqam (Arqam bin Abil Arqam). The person who proposed a reserve is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when wealth from Iraq arrived, Umar refused a suggestion to hold a reserve for future emergencies, saying he would not disobey Allaah today for tomorrow's dangers and would prepare for the Muslims as the Prophet had.
notes: Text ends mid-parenthesis ('obedience to Allaah and Rasulullaah'). The person who proposed a reserve is unnamed.

summary: Salamah bin Sa'eed reports that when Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf urged keeping a reserve, Umar said the idea came from Shaytaan, quoted the verse promising a way out for the one who has taqwa, and warned that Shaytaan's words would become a test for later generations.
Hasan narrates that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that he wished a day would come when the Baytul Maal was empty, so that Allaah would know he had given every person his right.
notes: Narrator 'Hadhrat Hasan' not matched (see n01099).

summary: Hasan reports that Umar wrote to Hudhayfah to pay everyone his dues; Hudhayfah replied that a large sum still remained, and Umar ordered it distributed, saying it was the people's property and belonged neither to him nor his family.
notes: Hudhayfa is matched to the bare approved entry hudhayfa; the text does not say which Hudhayfah. Narrator not matched (see n01099).

summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah Waalibi reports that when Ibn Nabbaaj told Ali the Baytul Maal was full of gold and silver, Ali distributed all of it to the people of Kufa and then prayed two rakaahs in the emptied treasury; Mujamma Taymi adds that Ali swept it and prayed there, hoping it would testify for him.
notes: Two reports joined: Ali bin Rabee'ah Waalibi, then Mujamma Taymi. The OCR gives 'All' for Ali in the first narrator's name. Ibn Nabbaaj is not in the vocabulary.

summary: Mu'aadh bin Alaa reports that Ali had received only one date container as his share and distributed the whole Baytul Maal; Antara Shaybaani reports Ali collecting from artisans and refusing to keep anything overnight; Abu Ubayd, through Antara, reports Qambar's hidden gold dish, which Ali weighed out and gave away.
notes: Three reports: Mu'aadh bin Alaa (from an unnamed grandfather), Antara Shaybaani, and Abu Ubayd (via Antara). Qambar is matched to the approved qambar, which is listed as unsure. Abu Ubayd is not matched to the vocabulary.

summary: Aslam reports Umar's consultation on who should receive the wealth, quoting the Qur'anic verses on the booty of the villages and the rights of the Muhaajireen and Ansaar.
Umar says the wealth belongs to more than those first named, including those who come after, citing the verse of prayer for the brothers who preceded them in Imaan.
notes: No narrator is named in the body; the 'Narration of Hadhrat Aslam' heading suggests Aslam but the text does not say so, so no narrator is tagged.

summary: Umar says there is no Muslim, even a shepherd in Aden, who has no right to the wealth.
notes: No narrator is named in the body; the heading names Aslam but the text does not, so none is tagged.

summary: Maalik bin Aws bin Hadathaan reports that Umar recited the verses on the recipients of zakaah and on the one-fifth share of spoils, and concluded that zakaah is reserved for those groups.
notes: The prophet is named inside the Qur'anic quotation ('Our slave Muhammad'). A footnote reference (Surah Hashr verse 9) is OCR debris.

summary: Umar recites the verses on the booty of the villages and on the Muhaajireen and Ansaar, and says the verse covers every Muslim, so each will receive his right even if he is a shepherd in the upper reaches of Yemen.
notes: The Qur'anic quotations are heavily garbled by OCR, but the meaning is intact.

summary: Su'da relates that Talha was distressed by wealth he did not know what to do with, so she advised him to give it to his family and tribe, and his treasurer later said the sum came to four hundred thousand.
notes: Su'da is the wife of Talha and is not in the vocabulary; she is tagged yes from the (RA) in the text. Su'da is the narrator and also the one who advises, so tagged as subject.

summary: Hasan reports that Talha sold a piece of land for seven hundred thousand, stayed awake all night for fear of dying before giving it away, and distributed all of it at dawn.
notes: Narrator 'Hadhrat Hasan' not matched (see n01099).

summary: Su'da reports again that Talha was distressed over the accumulated wealth, distributed four hundred thousand to his family and tribe on her advice, and was given the title Talha Fayyaadh, the Very Generous.
notes: Same narrator as n01116.

summary: Sa'eed bin Abdul Azeez reports that Zubayr had a thousand slaves who earned for him, and he gave the earnings away every night so that nothing was left when he returned home.
notes: The narrator is not matched to any vocabulary entry.

summary: Mugheeth bin Sumay reports that although Zubayr's thousand slaves earned for him, not one dirham of their earnings entered his house, because he gave all of it to the needy.
notes: A stray OCR symbol at the end of the text is ignored.
